answers.explanation: Programs and data must be loaded into main memory before the CPU can use them.
Volatile storage forgets without power; nonvolatile storage remembers.
That's its purpose: a large, permanent extension of main memory.
Circular tracks are cut into sectors, the smallest unit the disk reads or writes.
It turns a request for a block into the physical work of moving heads and reading sectors.
SSDs are faster than hard disks precisely because nothing has to move.
Random access is the opposite of sequential access, where you have to go through the data in order, like a tape.
It's limited in size and forgets everything at power off, so secondary storage holds things long term.
